How Communion with the Earth works in a room

November 26, 2026 · By Kimberly Marnell

Communion with the Earth is the largest painting I have available: oil on canvas, 36 × 48 inches. At that size it doesn't decorate a wall, it sets the tone of the room. Here is how to tell whether your space is right for it, and how to hang it well.

Start with the wall, not the furniture

The painting is 48 inches wide and 36 inches tall. Before anything else, cut a piece of paper or cardboard to that size, or mark the four corners on the wall with painter's tape, and live with the outline for a day. Look at it from the doorway, from your usual seat and from across the room. A large painting should feel generous, not crowded: leave at least a hand's width of clear wall on each side of the outline and keep it clear of light switches, vents and door frames.

Above a sofa, console or bed

A common guide is for art over furniture to span about two-thirds of the furniture's width. At 48 inches wide, Communion with the Earth sits comfortably over a sofa, sideboard or bed of roughly 6 to 7 feet. Hang it so the bottom edge is about 8 to 10 inches above the back of the sofa or headboard, close enough that the painting and the furniture read as one group.

On an open wall with nothing beneath it, a usual starting point is to put the center of the painting about 57 to 60 inches from the floor, roughly eye level. With a 36-inch-tall canvas, that places the top edge around 75 to 78 inches up.

Colors it lives with

The painting is warm: a soft pink ground, a woman in rose-colored fabric, a cluster of yellow flowers and green foliage at the edges. It sits easily with cream, oatmeal and warm white walls, natural wood, linen and stone. The greens in the leaves pick up house plants and olive or sage textiles. You don't need to match it. One or two of its colors repeated in a pillow, a throw or a plant is enough to tie it to the room.

Light

Indirect daylight or a warm lamp brings out the luminous folds of the fabric. As with any oil painting, avoid a spot where strong direct sunlight falls on it for hours each day, and keep it away from heat sources such as radiators or a working fireplace mantel.

See it before you decide

The painting's page has room views, close-up details and a scale view beside a 5 ft 6 in figure. Open the photo viewer there to step through them. If you're unsure about your own wall, email me a straight-on photo of it with its width and ask.

The practical details

Communion with the Earth is $10,400 and sold unframed, with a signed certificate of authenticity and free insured shipping within the US. Major works are reserved by email and invoiced, so the first step is simply a conversation.
